active.title: Worktrees live at worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>, kinds by repo role, one name parser
active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `worktrees/<repo>/<M.m.p><letter>-<kind>` (`_NAME_RE`, `dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_kinds.py:32`) does not name the project; readers map a path to a context by repo-slug lookup or their own glob: the gate (`core/invocation.py:125-160`, `scope`/`repo_owner`), `dd-bug-resolution/scripts/_specs.py:44` (`*-{kind}`), doctor `check_worktrees` (filters by repo name), `hooks/ctx_inject.py:143-163`, the dead preflight and closure (`_release_phase.py:54-76`). `impl` reads the trio from the repo it opens in (`_worktree_new.py:35-43`), so an associated repo can never open `impl`; associated repos have no kind rule. Letter `_worktree_new.py:51-57`; version `_worktree_git.py:103-123` (`work_version`); `kind_for` (`_worktree_kinds.py:41`) has no production caller; ADRs 0097 and 0107 are both accepted for one shape. Change: `worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>` on branch `wt/<kind>-<M.m.p>-<letter>`; `.gitkeep` in `worktrees/<ctx>/<repo-slug>/` created by context create/alive/repo add, removed by dead/repo remove; letter = lowest free per repo and version over all kinds; kinds by role (main `impl|bug|backlog|release`, associated `impl|bug`; `impl` in an associated repo reads the trio of the main repo); one name parser (`_NAME_RE`) through which every reader passes (gate `invocation.scope`, the `_specs.py` glob, doctor, ctx_inject, closure, `rows()`/`ours()`); delete `kind_for`. The worktrees/ path patterns of ADRs 0114, 0129 and 0132 read through the same parser. Migration: upgrade refuses while any worktree sits in the old layout (`fix:` merge or clean). Done when: a context with an associated repo opens `impl` and `bug` in both repos and the gate scopes both to the context. Files: dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_{kinds,new,git,end}.py, worktree.py, core/invocation.py, features/spec_context/gate_policy.py, dd-bug-resolution/scripts/_specs.py, features/spec_context/doctor.py, hooks/ctx_inject.py, dd-release-implementation/scripts/_release_phase.py, features/spec_context/service.py (create/alive/dead/repo add/remove), worktrees/AGENTS.md. Bugs (class this closes: ownership guessed from a path that does not name the context): sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos, push-gate-own-repo-slug-not-excluded-from-a-git-worktree-outside-repos. ADR 0174 (proposed; supersedes 0097, 0107 at acceptance; reaffirms 0108).

active.description:
Measured (HEAD e83e55783): nothing shows a project's worktrees; the doctor (`features/spec_context/doctor.py:215-224`, `check_worktrees`) filters `worktree_rows` by the repo names of ALIVE contexts and `rows()` (`dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_git.py:156-203`) walks only registered repos, so ADR 0112's 'a worktree whose repo left the context' is never reported. Change: only `context show --json` (one context) gains `worktrees` per repo, derived from `worktree_rows` (one owner, ADR 0135), plus snapshots (`archive/wt/*` tags and the bundles in `.dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/`); `context list --json` stays unchanged and remains the gitflow source `rows()` reads (`_worktree_git.py:75-93`, ADR 0144), so nothing recurses. The doctor and ctx_inject use the same computation as `context show`; the doctor reports an orphan worktree (repo in no context, context DEAD). Zero state file (ADR 0108). ADD justified: no unit answers 'which worktrees does this project have'; the answer is derived, never stored, and `check_worktrees`' own repo-name filter is replaced by the shared computation instead of growing a second one. Done when: the same list comes out of `context show`, doctor and ctx_inject from one computation (ctx_inject already renders the doctor's, `hooks/ctx_inject.py:143-154`). active.title: Existing code migrates to the multi-platform-by-construction ADR, rules P1-P10, one sweep per rule
active.description:
Operator, 2026-10-07, verbatim: 'toda arquitetura e a forma como metodos são programados deve pensar em ser multi-plataforma'; 'tanto na lib, na CLI, nos scripts dentro de skills'; ADR accepted the same day: 'Aceito, com essa divisão (Recommended)'. The ADR has no id yet: decisions.jsonl on feature/0.5.0 and every rc-10 tree carries no multi-platform record (the rc-10 Reconciliation writes it through its lane). Decision: one codebase; OS facts live in one seam, dadaia_workspace/core/platform.py, and tooling refuses OS literals elsewhere. Rules: P1 platform.py is the only reader of sys.platform/os.name, venv dir and .exe via sysconfig; P2 never bare python/bash - sys.executable, executables via shutil.which; P3 list argv, shell=False, no shlex; P4 pathlib in code, as_posix only for display/compare, no '/' joins; P5 encoding='utf-8' on all text I/O incl. hook stdout, CI never masks with PYTHONUTF8; P6 rmtree onexc read-only handler, os.replace atomic writes, no exec bit/symlink reliance; P7 one renderer for printed commands (core/cli_line), never &&, $VAR, sudo, chmod +x; P8 git and harness hooks are a one-line #!/bin/sh shim exec'ing the absolute interpreter, logic in Python; P9 shipped law names commands once, neutral, rendered per platform at install; P10 ruff PTH, S602, S605, PLW1514, a guard refusing OS literals outside the seam, Windows+macOS CI = Linux selection, .gitattributes eol. Split (ruled): rc-10 bug batch takes the 8 Windows bugs, shipped-law-hardcodes-the-posix-venv-path (P9) and CI selection parity (P10 CI part); this entry is the rc-11 rest - hook shims (P8), pre-push in Python, lint + guard (P10), path joins (P4), one command renderer (P7). Design: one sweep per P-rule over dadaia_workspace/ (lib, CLI, skill scripts), each sweep lands with its repo guard (the P10 OS-literal guard or the named ruff rule) turned on in the same job so the rule cannot regress; each sweep's commit carries its git grep line and hit count. Open (to the PLAN): how skill scripts get command lines without a second decider - relay the CLI's rendered output. Placement rc-11 is the operator's split; every other design detail not quoted from a ruling is agent default, unruled.

Scope grill 2026-10-11 (operator, verbatim): 'Tudo, P8 relativo (Recommended)'. Earlier rulings kept: 2026-10-07 'windows deve satisfazer as mesmas necessidades que linux ... toda arquitetura ... multi-plataforma. porra'; 'tanto na lib, na CLI, nos scripts dentro de skills'; ADR 0220 'Aceito, com essa divisão (Recommended)'. Destination: 0.6.0 (grill roadmap-050 Q2; was 0.5.0). Wave: 3 (platform sweep over the clean Wave 2 base). Scope now: ADR 0220's second half complete: the verify shlex bug (verify-line-shlex-mangles-windows-paths), PYTHONUTF8 out of the cross-OS CI (cross-os-ci-masks-utf8), the pre-push generated in Python with the bash script deleted, the P10 rules in the existing ruff select, one line in the existing guard (standalone scripts resolved with the end of the kernel copies), and P8's relative interpreter lookup by an ADR amendment.

active.title: A reviewer's verdict survives a worktree sync when the lane's own reviewed patch is unchanged
active.description: Target 0.6.0. Arm A, not a bug: today's contract is designed and holds. worktrees/AGENTS.md §2 accepts only the equivalent reviewed patch series with a matching diff_sha256, and specs/memory/product/sdd/worktrees.md:34 says a tree whose patch context a sync changed needs a fresh verdict and no verdict is rebound. Cost measured in the rc-22 lanes on 2026-10-21: each merge onto the work branch forced a sync of the sibling lanes, then a reviewer re-verdict on every lane whose diff context moved; at least 8 re-verdicts that day, about 1 to 4 minutes of reviewer time each (read from the reviewer hand-backs' durations). Adjacent BUGS.jsonl appends also made syncs conflict, and the main thread rebuilt 3 lanes (the ledger-append conflict is rc18-review-loose-ends item 8). Gain: fewer review round-trips. Trade-off: the verdict gate is the review trust boundary the operator closed in rc-22 (Q5), so loosening its binding is a security surface. Constraint on any design: the verdict stays bound to the lane's reviewed patch and never covers code the reviewer did not judge; a sync that changes the lane's own patch still needs a fresh verdict. History the grill must weigh: rc-18 AC4.7 built a manual verdict rebind and the operator dropped it ('Drop the rebind (Recommended)'), so the rebind was reverted (rc-18 SPEC AC4.7 ruling). Design left open for the grill. No new gate.
active.provenance: Operator demand 2026-10-21, grill Q15 on keeping a reviewer's verdict across a worktree sync when the lane's own patch is unchanged: "Backlog do 0.6.0 (Recommended)"

active.title: OpenCode harness support in the product, and an OpenCode lane in the eval pipeline
active.description: Target 0.5.0, after rc-23. Exit condition: the operator validates the rc-23 eval pipeline (R1: 'Open Code vamos configurar depois que eu sentir que vc sabe construir ... um pipeline de eval'); only then is this entry picked. Scope: (1) product support: a registry row in dadaia_workspace/core/harness_registry.py, a persona transcode to .opencode/agents/<name>.md, and a hook projection as .opencode/plugins/*.js that spawns the projected hook wrappers; (2) an OpenCode leg in eval.yml's matrix at the same floors, with a forged-verdict identity rule in compare.py. Facts, measured locally on opencode 1.14.33: it reads AGENTS.md, .agents/skills and .claude/skills; it lists .opencode/agents/*.md (frontmatter mode: subagent) as subagents in 'opencode agent list'; a plugin in .opencode/plugins/ can block a tool call by throwing in tool.execute.before. Unverified: the plugin behaviour in headless mode (opencode run) and the subagent identity in its transcript, so subagent_key stays unset and the eval's forged check would be that harness's only verdict guard until verified; the first task is a read-only check against the live binary. Estimate: about 200-250 source lines and 300-400 test lines, 8-10 tasks, two jobs (registry row and personas; hook plugin). History: OpenCode support was removed once (v0.1.24, opencode_runtime deleted; histo shared-headless-adapter-base), and ADR 0020 governs roster growth, naming cursor, devin and copilot only, so adding OpenCode is a roster decision the operator rules. Open for the grill: the lane's auth and model (agent default, unruled: a provider API key with openai/gpt-6.1-sol; cost unmeasured).

active.title: A wt-backlog lane also lands a repo's top-level references/ folder (research notes, open-access PDFs), one review, no verify: run
active.description: Measured (HEAD e0d333ab8): a backlog lane's merge refuses every path outside specs/ and the repo's AGENTS.md (_check_specs_only, dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_end.py:169-174; law: worktrees-AGENTS.md:23, lane 3); repos/ is merge-only (root AGENTS.md §3); a wt-main opens only in IMPLEMENTATION and a candidate needs scope that changes behaviour, so a docs-only folder of reference material that agents read while refining specs has no lane. Outcome: the lightest lane carries a repo's top-level references/ — preferably wt-backlog-* itself (_check_specs_only and lane 3 also accept references/), else one named lane — with one review and no verify: run, so a project versions its reference material. Out of scope: any change to what .dadaia/references/ is. Interim: the material lives in .dadaia/references/connect-ideas/ (outside git) and moves to the repo root once this lands.
